study_identification.title: Gray matter atrophy is constrained by normal structural brain network architecture in depression

study_characteristics.study_objective: Test whether individual-level gray matter atrophy patterns in depression are constrained by normal connectome architecture; identify patient-specific and shared disease epicenters; examine vulnerability of regions connected to epicenters and whether connectome–atrophy association reveals homogeneous subgroups.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Per-patient stepwise linear regression using connectivity maps of putative epicenters to explain regional atrophy (R2); model comparison across structural/functional single vs multi-epicenter variants (paired t-tests); Pearson correlation between disease exposure (connectivity-weighted epicenter proximity) and regional Z-scores with FDR correction; k-means clustering (repeated 100×; silhouette-based K selection) on per-patient connectivity–atrophy correlations to derive two subgroups and compare age of onset.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Structural multi-epicenter connectome profiles explain substantial variance in individual GMV atrophy in depression, highlighting shared epicenters (e.g., hippocampus, thalamus, medial frontal gyrus), greater vulnerability of strongly connected regions, and two subgroups differing in age of onset.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across patients, structural multi-epicenter models explained 44% ± 16% of variance in GMV atrophy and outperformed single-epicenter and functional models (all paired t-tests p < 0.001). Patients averaged 8.45 ± 2.97 epicenters; several were significantly shared (e.g., thalamus, hippocampus, medial frontal gyrus) and showed higher participation coefficients. Regions with higher disease exposure exhibited greater atrophy (mean Pearson R = 0.50 ± 0.12; FDR-corrected p < 0.05). The approach identified two subgroups with a significant difference in age of onset (two-sample t = 2.48; FDR p = 0.044; Cohen’s d = 0.49). Replication analyses reproduced main findings with medicated patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Limited clinical data prevented deeper links between connectome–atrophy association and symptoms; exclusion of comorbid disorders limits generalizability; replication patients were medicated and medication details were not recorded, precluding analysis of medication effects.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Uses individualized normative modeling (GPR) to derive per-region Z-scores; compares single vs multi-epicenter structural and functional models; controls for spatial proximity with a ‘spatial disease exposure’ analysis; subgrouping via repeated k-means on connectivity–atrophy correlations.

general_notes.general_notes: Atlas reported as 246-region; some sections reference 242 × 242 networks (likely minor parcel exclusions). Acquisition on 3T GE MR750 with detailed parameters per dataset. No explicit site/scanner harmonization (e.g., ComBat/HBR) reported; normative predictors limited to age and sex. Abstract states 297 patients vs Table counts totaling 211; analyses and Table 1 support 105 + 106 = 211 patients and 130 + 126 = 256 HCs.
